moe.routing.qwen3_30b_a3b.c16384.s1024.d.note: How many distinct experts a block of 1024 consecutive positions touches in one mixture layer of Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B, measured on 1 prompt(s) of 16384 positions from the harness's eval corpus: the mean over the 48 mixture layers and the 16 block(s) each prompt divides into, 768 blocks in all, spread 46 to 119. This is the quantity assumption.cost_model.moe_routing assumes: the routed matmuls a segment builds, and so the weights its preprocessed trace holds.

What the assumption gives for the same block: E (1 - (1 - k/E)^S) at E = 128, k = 8, S = 1024, which is exact_cells.expected_distinct_experts. It is beside the measured entry so the two are read together and neither is a second measurement of the other.

moe.routing.qwen3_30b_a3b.c16384.s512.to.note: The busiest routed matmul of a block of 512 positions: the tokens the most-used expert of a mixture layer took, meaned over the 48 layers and the 1536 blocks. Under assumption.cost_model.moe_routing every routed matmul of this block covers 32 tokens (exact_cells.routed_blocks at E = 128, k = 8, S = 512); a measured block is laid out from its own histogram, which runs/<run>/routing.json carries in full. That flat figure is what the model BUILDS and not what a uniform draw's busiest expert takes, which is higher than the share for the same reason any multinomial maximum is: read this against the histogram, not against the share.
